question: What exactly is the market benchmark we score against
why_it_blocks: Every gate that mentions closing line value needs a price we are allowed to store and publish
answer_now: No usable benchmark for 2026: the mirror carries a closing line for 137 of 148 played games and no timestamp; opening prices exist for 2021 only
what_would_close_it: A dated, hashed capture of one agreed consensus page, twice per week, kept for 4 weeks

question: Do we have the right to store operator prices at all
why_it_blocks: If not, the leaderboard cannot use CLV and must fall back to proper scores alone
answer_now: Unverified. No terms were read for the aggregate mirror; the league page for odds does not exist (nfl.com/odds returns 404)
what_would_close_it: A read of the source terms recorded in docs/SOURCES.md

question: Does an official depth chart exist anywhere in the league
why_it_blocks: Three requirements (register, group slots, stale-row flags) all assume one
answer_now: No. nfl.com has no depth-chart page; club charts are captioned unofficial by the clubs
what_would_close_it: An official artefact that names strings, or a decision to use playing time as the definition

question: Is playing time or listed rank the depth definition
why_it_blocks: It decides whether the backup-deficiency feature can be built at all
answer_now: Recommendation: playing time, because it is measurable and already wrong in the club charts (149 slots carry more than one rank-1 player)
what_would_close_it: Snap-share series per team-position-week from CI

question: How much is a missing starter actually worth
why_it_blocks: A fixed penalty is the single most common modelling error in this space
answer_now: Measured: -0.485 points per expected-miss on the margin, 95% CI [-0.719, -0.251], n=2,367 games (2016-2024). A -3.0 point penalty is far outside the interval
what_would_close_it: Nothing further for the aggregate; per-position coefficients remain unestimated

question: What does Questionable mean on a given field
why_it_blocks: The label is a feature or it is noise depending on the answer
answer_now: Measured on 2016-2024: Questionable plays 64.46% of the time (CI 63.64-65.28, n=13,131); Out 0.02% (n=8,736); Doubtful 0.92% (n=1,522)
what_would_close_it: Nothing; the level may now be replaced by the surprise delta

question: Does 'not listed' mean available
why_it_blocks: No. If it does, the availability feed is complete; if it does not, every absent-but-healthy assumption in earlier work is wrong
answer_now: No. The report mirror carries only Out/Questionable/Probable/Doubtful; a player on reserve is simply absent (0 reserve rows in 42,179)

question: Are parlays priceable from independence at all
why_it_blocks: Ranking a parlay on multiplied marginals is invalid if the legs correlate
answer_now: Same-game side and total legs are near independent in the mirror (phi 0.013, n=2,927) so independence is roughly adequate there; prop legs are unmeasured because no prop prices exist
what_would_close_it: Prop prices plus a joint outcome feed

question: What is our sample until a skill claim is defensible
why_it_blocks: Under-powered leaderboards are the fastest way to publish noise
answer_now: Quantified: at -110 (break-even 52.38%) detecting a 55% bettor at 80% power needs about 2,243 bets; 57% needs 719. On proper scores, 200 graded singles is the escrow floor we chose
what_would_close_it: Nothing; the number is frozen in the pre-registration

question: Which week-10 fixture results are official
why_it_blocks: A feed with a wrong score poisons the ratings for weeks afterward
answer_now: 148 of 150 fixtures reconcile exactly to the official standings on W-L-T and PF/PA (32/32 teams). PIT@CIN and LAC@BAL were not final at capture and are carried blank
what_would_close_it: A later capture of the same schedule page

question: Is the venue in the data the venue that was played
why_it_blocks: Totals, weather and rest all hang off the venue
answer_now: Partly: the mirror carries Melbourne Cricket Ground for the Week 1 international game, so it does track some venues; the Munich fixture is absent from the mirror and the schedule page's own ticketing widget for that fixture names the home club's stadium

question: Do we hold any licensed game-level starter data
why_it_blocks: The brief asks for game books; the site currently has none
answer_now: No. The sample game book carries an explicit media-only copyright notice
what_would_close_it: A licence, or a decision to derive starters from playing time only

question: Where do immutable captures live
why_it_blocks: A static Pages site cannot be the system of record for a growing snapshot history
answer_now: Decided for this section: raw bodies out of the published tree, hashes and counts committed; a real object store still needs the owner
what_would_close_it: An object-store choice and an alert channel

question: Who reconciles six sections into one story
why_it_blocks: Six sections publish the same fixtures at different tiers, which is how a reader gets fooled
answer_now: This section publishes a readiness register keyed to the brief's own requirement list so the reader can see the gate on every line
what_would_close_it: Owner decision on adopting one hub
